champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency
ordered_diagnoses: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive skin laxity with flexural papules and calcification of elastic fibers
salient_findings: Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas
Severe skin sagging with loss of elasticity
Excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
key_facts: 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
Asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas since early childhood
Severe skin sagging occurred on the abdomen with loss of elasticity
Skin symptoms spread extensively with developmental growth
No extracutaneous involvement
Born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
Younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds)
Echocardiographic examination results were normal
Fundoscopic examination results were normal
Histopathology showed excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments in the reticular dermis
Genetic testing revealed compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene

shortlist: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

shortlist.label: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive skin laxity, yellowish papules, and calcification of elastic fibers matches this condition

shortlist.label: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's low clotting activity of factor X and prolonged prothrombin time, along with skin symptoms, suggest this rare condition

shortlist.label: Cutis laxa
shortlist.why_kept: Severe skin sagging and loss of elasticity are characteristic of cutis laxa, although the presence of yellowish papules and calcification of elastic fibers are more suggestive of pseudoxanthoma elasticum

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: While Ehlers-Danlos syndrome can present with skin hyperextensibility and joint hypermobility, the specific features of yellowish papules and calcification of elastic fibers are not typical of this condition

shortlist.label: Gerodermia osteodysplastica
shortlist.why_kept: This condition is characterized by skin laxity and osteodysplasia, but the patient's lack of extracutaneous involvement and normal imaging studies make it a less likely diagnosis

s4.champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency

raw.champion: Pseudoxanthoma elasticum-like disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency
raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of progressive skin laxity, yellowish coalesced papules in flexural areas, and histopathology showing excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments are consistent with pseudoxanthoma elasticum. However, the additional findings of low clotting activity of factor X and prolonged prothrombin time, along with the genetic testing revealing compound heterozygous sequence variation in the GGCX gene, suggest a disorder with multiple coagulation factor deficiency.

rejected.label: Cutis laxa
rejected.why: No mention of coagulation abnormalities and different histopathological features

rejected.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: Different clinical and histopathological features, such as hypermobile joints and tissue fragility

rejected.label: Gerodermia osteodysplastica
rejected.why: Typically presents with osteodysplasia and distinct facial features, which are not mentioned in the vignette
